findings.title: Readiness probe can throw and abort the whole fix plan
findings.description: `checkoutReadiness` handles failures from the first two git probes, but not the later steps. `realpathSync(topLevel)` and `realpathSync(checkoutPath)` can throw, for example if the directory vanishes between `existsSync` and the call. The `rev-parse --git-path` call and each `git status --porcelain` call are also unguarded. Any of these rejections propagates out of `gateByReadiness` and `planRoutedFixes`, so one broken non-invoking checkout, a timeout or a lock aborts the entire fix run. The design says such checkouts should be deferred with a reason, and no `DeferReason` covers a probe failure. Map unexpected probe failures to an explicit deferral. Alternatively, catch them, log at ERROR level, and rethrow with the checkout path in the message.

findings.title: Plan/apply wiring is duplicated between CLI and MCP
findings.description: The `scopeViews` construction, the `runCheck` selector, the `resolveInvokingCheckout` guard (only when more than one view) and the `planRoutedFixes` then `applyFixPlan` sequence are written out twice. They appear in `check.ts:172-198` and `runRoutedFix`, and again in `workflowTools.ts`. The `fileSlice: \`${n}-slice\`` literal is also repeated. The two copies can drift, and the PR's own premise is parity between them. Move the shared sequence into a core helper such as `runRoutedFix({ project, views, checker, scope })`, with the prompt step injected by the CLI.

findings.title: Non-null assertions on `fixAction` instead of a narrowed type
findings.description: `fixRelPath` and `routeView` use `finding.fixAction!` (`fixReport.ts` falls back with `?.` instead). The code is safe today only because `fixableOf` filters on `f.fixAction`, but `gateByReadiness` is exported and takes unfiltered `ConsistencyFinding[]`. A caller that passes a finding without a `fixAction` gets a runtime TypeError. The typescript rule treats `as` and `!` as a smell. Introduce a `FixableFinding = ConsistencyFinding & { fixAction: NonNullable<…> }` type and a guard, and use it in these signatures.

findings.title: Output mode selected by a display flag, not by result shape
findings.description: `printCheckOutput` chooses the routed report with `fixRes && showWorktree`. `showWorktree` means "views carry worktree attribution", and it is also used to prefix findings. The data that actually drives the routed report is `deferred`, `commits` and `fixLog[].worktree`. If the attribution rule changes (for example, only some views get a worktree), the summary path will silently change. Derive the mode from the result, for example by checking whether `fixRes.commits` or `fixRes.deferred` is non-empty or any `fixLog` entry has a `worktree`.

findings.title: Test helpers exported from test files; cross-package relative imports
findings.description: `routedFixes.test.ts` exports `designPath`, `tasksPath`, `completeBeta`, `worktreeCtx`, `createRoutedSetup`, `dryRun`, `aboutSubject` and `RoutedSetup` from a `*.test.ts` file. Nothing in the diff imports them, and `createProjectFor` at the bottom of the file reads the module-level `setup` implicitly. Move shared pieces into `tests/helpers/` and drop the `export` from anything that isn't shared. The CLI and MCP tests import `../../../core/tests/helpers/gitWorktreeFixture.js` across package boundaries. That works, but it couples package test trees. A shared test-utils location would be cleaner.

findings.title: Lost error cause when rethrowing as UserError
findings.description: `runRoutedFix` catches the `resolveInvokingCheckout` error and throws `new UserError(err.message)` without `cause`. The original git failure, which `resolveInvokingCheckout` attaches via `{ cause: err }`, is dropped. Pass `{ cause: err }` if `UserError` supports it. If it doesn't, this is acceptable because the message is already user-facing.

findings.title: `checker.fix` / `checker.fixAll` may now be unreferenced
findings.description: Both consumers now use `check`/`checkAll` plus `applyFixes`. The mocks for `fix`/`fixAll` were removed from the CLI and MCP tests. If no other callers exist, those public methods are dead code, and they bypass routing, so they invite misuse. I did not verify other callers.

findings.title: Single-checkout `restoredfix` accounting
findings.description: After a failed commit and a successful restore, `fixed -= fixLog.length` and `fixLog = []` is correct, and test case 5 covers it. In the failed-restore case the entries intentionally remain, as test 7 asserts. This behaviour is acceptable.
